status: Protocol published, zero values measured. Every measured_value below is null because there is no set of settled bets to measure on (Q-PRICE-01, Q-PRICE-03).

policy.rule: Correlations are computed only from officially sourced numbers, and n is published with every value.
policy.what_counts_as_official_input: Settlement outcomes and market prices taken from a licensed or permitted source. Model probabilities are not an official number and are never used to estimate a correlation.
policy.why_n_is_published: A correlation without n is unfalsifiable. At n=30 nearly any value is consistent with zero, and publishing it invites exactly the parlay pricing it should forbid.
policy.minimum_n_status: Proposed default. The owner may raise it; the builder refuses to render a value below whatever floor is set (Q-PRICE-03).
policy.clustering: Bets on the same game are not independent. Intervals come from a bootstrap clustered by game, not from an i.i.d. formula.
policy.what_a_correlation_is_not: A correlation coefficient is not a joint probability, not a conditional probability and not a causal effect. It does not license multiplying marginals.

estimators.name: Phi coefficient
estimators.use: Two binary outcomes, e.g. two sides both covering
estimators.formula_note: Phi on the 2x2 table of settlement outcomes

estimators.name: Excess joint probability
estimators.use: The quantity that actually matters for pricing a combo
estimators.formula_note: P(A and B) observed minus P(A) x P(B). This is the dependence premium, and it is the number a combo price must reflect.

estimators.name: Game-clustered bootstrap interval
estimators.use: Uncertainty on both of the above
estimators.formula_note: Resample games, not bets, so correlated legs inside one game do not fake extra information.

pairs.why_it_matters: The classic same-game parlay pair. If the favourite covers, the total is often carried by the same scoring, so the pair is not independent.
Near-duplicate legs sold as a two-leg parlay. The joint probability is bounded by the moneyline probability, which is the check that a product of marginals fails.

pairs.leg_b: Leading rusher over his rushing prop
pairs.why_it_matters: Prop combo. Game script couples the two, and the operator's void rules for an injury scratch decide what 'settled' even means.

pairs.leg_b: Team B covers in a different game
pairs.why_it_matters: The cross-game parlay. Dependence here should be near zero; if it is not, something shared (weather, a late news event) is moving both and the pricing assumption is wrong.
Two views of the same offensive output sold as independent legs.

pairs.leg_a: Two sides in the same 1pm window
pairs.why_it_matters: Window-level correlation. If a shared late injury or weather event moves several games at once, a same-window parlay is not the independent product it is priced as.
The mirror of C-01. Measuring both is the check that the estimator is symmetric and not fitting one direction.

pairs.leg_a: A key starter ruled Out before kickoff
pairs.why_it_matters: The personnel-availability pair. Without it, any claim that injuries move a line is an assertion. It also requires a verified replacement to interpret (Q-DEPTH-01).
The surprise pair. It requires multi-day snapshots (Q-SNAPSHOT-01) and a price series (Q-PRICE-01), so it is the last of the set to become measurable.

pairs.leg_a: Two games in the same stadium on consecutive days
pairs.why_it_matters: Surface and venue wear. Included so a venue effect, if any, is measured rather than asserted.
The weather pair. Blocked until the roof designation and NWS capture exist (Q-WX-01), because a closed roof removes the effect entirely.

measurement_plan: 1. Answer Q-PRICE-01 and Q-PRICE-03 so there is a price series and an agreed n floor.
2. Build the settlement ledger: every bet, its market, its price at forecast time, its closing price, and its outcome, keyed by game_id.
3. Estimate phi and the excess joint probability for each pair, with a game-clustered bootstrap interval.
4. Publish n alongside every value. A pair below the floor is published as 'not measured at this n', never as a number.
5. Only then may the joint-evidence gate open for that specific pair, and only for that pair.
